questions.question: Read the passage and answer the question. A small payments bank expanded into semi-urban markets after it noticed that merchants wanted simple settlement tools, transparent charges and local-language support. Instead of opening large branches, it trained local agents and built a mobile dashboard for daily reconciliations. What was the bank's main strategic focus?

options.A: Replacing all agents with large branches
options.E: Solving merchant pain points through digital and local support

questions.explanation: The passage highlights simple settlement tools, transparent charges, local-language support, agents and a dashboard.

questions.question: Read the passage and answer the question. The same bank grew because shopkeepers trusted agents who could explain failed transfers and settlement delays. The author implies that technology adoption improves when:

options.B: users receive clear human support along with digital tools
options.C: customers are forced to use apps without help

questions.explanation: The passage links adoption to trusted agents who explain digital issues.

questions.question: In the passage about the payments bank, which word is closest in meaning to 'transparent'?
questions.explanation: Transparent charges are charges that are clear and easy to understand.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate pair of words: The branch manager handled the complaint with _______ and gave the customer a _______ timeline for resolution.
questions.explanation: The sentence needs a positive handling quality and a believable timeline.

questions.question: The new savings plan was _______ for young earners because it offered liquidity without _______ long-term discipline.
questions.explanation: A suitable plan can offer liquidity while not weakening discipline.

questions.question: Choose the best replacement: By the time the audit will begin, the documents will have been uploaded.
questions.explanation: After 'by the time' for a future reference, use present simple: the audit begins.

questions.question: Choose the best replacement: Neither of the cashiers have closed their counter.
questions.explanation: 'Neither of' is singular in this construction, so use 'has'.

questions.question: Choose the best replacement: Had I knew about the service charge, I would have selected another account.
questions.explanation: The correct inversion is 'Had I known'.

questions.question: Choose the best word for blank (A): Digital lending has seen a _______ rise, but responsible underwriting remains essential.
questions.explanation: A rise can be significant; the other words do not fit naturally.

questions.question: Choose the best word for blank (C): Better account aggregation can _______ transparency in retail borrowing.
questions.explanation: A system can promote transparency.

questions.question: Four words may be incorrectly placed. Choose the correct interchange: The bank must first (A) understanding customer (B) strengths and have an accurate (C) embrace of their (D) needs.
questions.explanation: The meaningful sentence is: embrace customer needs and have an accurate understanding of their strengths.

questions.question: Choose the correct interchange: The technology at our (A) detail can automate (B) streamline tasks and (C) mundane operations that require attention to (D) disposal.
questions.explanation: Correct sense: technology at our disposal can automate mundane tasks and streamline operations.

questions.question: Rearrange the parts to form a coherent sentence: A. to help customers compare loans B. the regulator asked lenders C. before accepting the offer D. to display the annual percentage rate clearly
questions.explanation: The sentence is: The regulator asked lenders to display the annual percentage rate clearly to help customers compare loans before accepting the offer.

questions.question: Find the segment with an error: The startup founder (A)/ was confident that his idea (B)/ was more superior (C)/ than any other option. (D)
questions.explanation: 'Superior' already expresses comparison; 'more superior' is incorrect.

questions.question: Find the segment with an error: Neither the officer (A)/ nor the clerks (B)/ was aware of (C)/ the revised schedule. (D)
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'clerks': were aware.

questions.question: Find the segment with an error: The borrower (A)/ was accused for (B)/ submitting false documents (C)/ during verification. (D)
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is 'accused of', not 'accused for'.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.

options.B: The guidelines aims to promote road safety.
options.D: The rescue team was able to save everyone trapped in the collapsed tunnel.
options.E: The tourists were exciting to see the Northern Lights.

questions.explanation: Only the correct answer has proper adjective and subject-verb agreement.

questions.question: Select the best word: Water _______ in drought-hit areas has pushed governments to invest in desalination.
questions.explanation: Water scarcity means shortage of water.

questions.question: Select the best word: She accepted the new role with great _______, eager to contribute fresh ideas.
questions.explanation: Enthusiasm fits the positive eagerness in the sentence.

questions.question: Select the best word: Many people _______ success comes quickly, but it often requires years of effort.
questions.explanation: Assume means believe without proof.

questions.question: Choose the correct alternative: The spike in housing prices has led many first-time buyers to postponing their plans indefinitely.
questions.explanation: 'Led someone to' is followed by the base verb: to postpone.

questions.question: Choose the correct alternative: The footage obtained from the drone was not being admissible in court.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'admissible' takes 'was not admissible'.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'bring up' correctly? I. She brought up the issue in the meeting. II. They brought up the old boxes from the basement. III. Her aunt brought her up.
questions.explanation: 'Bring up' can mean mention, bring upstairs, or raise a child.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'look after' correctly? I. She stayed home to look after her brother. II. The manager promised to look after the complaints. III. He wanted to look after the documents before signing.
questions.explanation: 'Look after' means take care of or handle. It does not mean examine documents.

questions.question: Match the sentence starters with correct endings. A. Amidst challenges, a glimmer of hope emerged B. Before sleep, dreams painted vivid landscapes C. Beneath the starlit sky, the rhythmic sounds. Endings: D. echoed through the quiet valley E. of unexplored possibilities and aspirations F. while old fears seemed vulnerable.
questions.explanation: Dreams painted landscapes of possibilities; sounds echoed through the valley.

questions.question: Choose the connector that best joins the ideas: Digital payments are convenient. They require stronger fraud awareness among new users.

options.A: Although digital payments are convenient, they require stronger fraud awareness among new users.
options.B: Because digital payments are convenient, they require no fraud awareness.
options.C: Digital payments are convenient unless they require awareness.
options.D: Digital payments require awareness so they are never convenient.

questions.explanation: Although shows contrast between convenience and the need for caution.

questions.question: Approximate the value: 39.8% of 810 + 24.9% of 640.
questions.explanation: Approximate as 40% of 810 plus 25% of 640 = 324 + 160 = 484, closest to 480.

questions.question: Find the missing number: 12, 18, 30, 54, 102, ?
questions.explanation: Differences are 6, 12, 24, 48, so next difference is 96.

questions.question: Find the wrong number: 7, 14, 42, 168, 672, 5040.
questions.explanation: The multipliers should be 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. After 168, the term should be 840, not 672.

questions.question: A table shows total pencils and total price. Shop A has 38 pencils worth Rs. 490. Wooden pencils cost Rs. 5 and mechanical pencils cost Rs. 20. How many mechanical pencils are in Shop A?
questions.explanation: Let mechanical pencils be x. 20x + 5(38 - x) = 490, so x = 20.

questions.question: Shop B has 47 pencils worth Rs. 415. Wooden pencils cost Rs. 5 and mechanical pencils cost Rs. 20. Find the number of wooden pencils.
questions.explanation: Let mechanical pencils be x. 20x + 5(47 - x) = 415, so x = 12 mechanical and 35 wooden.

questions.question: Shop C has 112 pencils worth Rs. 1310. Wooden pencils cost Rs. 5 and mechanical pencils cost Rs. 20. Mechanical pencils are approximately what percent of total pencils?
questions.explanation: 20x + 5(112 - x) = 1310 gives x = 50. Mechanical share = 50/112 = 44.64%, approximately 45%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article 30% above cost price and gives a 20% discount. Find the profit percentage.
questions.explanation: If CP = 100, MP = 130, SP = 104. Profit = 4%.

questions.question: A and B can complete a work in 15 and 24 days. They work together for 4 days, then C completes the remaining work in 17 days. In how many days can C alone complete 50% of the work?
questions.explanation: A+B do 4(1/15 + 1/24) = 13/30. Remaining 17/30 is done by C in 17 days, so C does full work in 30 days and half in 15 days.

questions.question: A 600 m train crosses a 300 m bridge in 18 seconds. Train B runs at half A's speed and is 25% shorter than A. How long will B take to cross the same bridge?
questions.explanation: Train A speed = 900/18 = 50 m/s. B speed = 25 m/s, B length = 450 m. Time = (450 + 300)/25 = 30 seconds.

questions.question: A person invests Rs. X at 6% simple interest for 5 years and earns Rs. 1500 interest. If he invests 3X at 10% compound interest for 2 years, find the amount.
X's present age is 50% more than Y's. Z's age is the average of X and Y. The difference between Z after 5 years and Y three years ago is 10 years. Find X's age after 6 years.
questions.explanation: Let Y = y, X = 1.5y, Z = 1.25y. (1.25y + 5) - (y - 3) = 10 gives y = 8, X = 12, after 6 years = 18.

questions.question: A spends 50% of income on rent, 20% of remaining on food, 10% of income on travelling and saves Rs. 10800. If B's income is 25% less than A's, find 60% of B's income.
questions.explanation: Food is 20% of the remaining 50%, i.e. 10% of income. Total spent = 70%, so savings = 30% = 10800. A = 36000, B = 27000, and 60% of B = 16200.

questions.question: The ratio of weights A:B is 1:2 and A:C is 2:3. If the average weight of A, B and C is 18 kg, find B's weight.
questions.explanation: Let A = 2x, B = 4x and C = 3x. Total = 9x = 54, x = 6, so B = 24 kg.

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 92 cm and length:breadth = 14:9. If a square's side is 2 cm more than the breadth, find the square's perimeter.
questions.explanation: 2(l+b)=92, so l+b=46. Ratio parts 23, so one part=2. Breadth=18, square side=20, perimeter=80.

questions.question: A value increases from 480 to 600. What is the percentage increase?
questions.explanation: Increase = 120. Percentage increase = 120/480 x 100 = 25%.

questions.question: The average of five numbers is 42. If one number 50 is removed, what is the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.explanation: Total = 210. Remaining total = 160. Average = 160/4 = 40.

questions.question: A boat travels 30 km downstream in 2 hours and 18 km upstream in 3 hours. Find the speed of the stream.
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 15, upstream speed = 6. Stream speed = (15 - 6)/2 = 4.5 km/h.

questions.question: A bag has 5 red, 4 blue and 3 green balls. One ball is drawn. What is the probability that it is not green?
questions.explanation: Not green balls = 9 out of 12, so probability = 3/4.

questions.question: How many 3-letter codes can be formed from A, B, C, D, E without repetition?
questions.explanation: The count is 5P3 = 5 x 4 x 3 = 60.

questions.question: A company manufactured 400 items and sold 320. Another company manufactured 300 and sold 250. Find the ratio of unsold items of the first to unsold items of the second.
questions.explanation: Unsold items are 80 and 50, ratio = 8:5.

questions.question: In a branch, 60% of 250 savings accounts and 40% of 180 current accounts are active. Find total active accounts.
A vendor buys 7 shirts at the marked price of 6 shirts and sells each after 4% discount on marked price. Find profit percentage.
questions.explanation: If MP of each is 100, CP for 7 = 600 and SP = 7 x 96 = 672. Profit = 72/600 x 100 = 12%.

questions.question: Pipe A fills a tank in 16 min and B in 24 min. Both work for 4 min. Then A's rate doubles and B's rate halves. How many more minutes are needed?
questions.explanation: First 4 minutes fill 5/12. New rate = 1/8 + 1/48 = 7/48. Remaining 7/12 takes 4 minutes.

questions.question: If x + y = 12 and xy = 32, find x^2 + y^2.
Tea costing Rs. 240/kg is mixed with tea costing Rs. 320/kg in the ratio 3:2. Find the average cost per kg.
questions.explanation: Weighted average = (240x3 + 320x2)/5 = 272.

questions.question: Eight persons A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H live on floors 1 to 8 from bottom to top. G lives three floors above D. Only two persons live below D. E lives immediately above H. C lives above H but below G. A lives above Manager-equivalent floor 5. Who lives on floor 5?
questions.explanation: D is on floor 3, G is on floor 6, and the remaining conditions place C on floor 5.

questions.question: Eight persons sit around a square table. A, C, E and G sit at corners facing inside; B, D, F and H sit at sides facing outside. G is opposite C. B sits immediately right of C. F sits opposite B. Who sits opposite A?
questions.explanation: The corner positions pair opposite corners. With G opposite C, the remaining opposite corner pair is A and E.

questions.question: Six candidates A to F have interviews from Monday to Saturday. B is immediately before D. A is after C but before F. E is not on Monday or Saturday. If C is on Monday, who is interviewed on Friday?
questions.explanation: A valid sequence is C, E, B, D, A, F. Therefore A is interviewed on Friday.

questions.question: Statements: P > Q = R, S >= T < Q, U < P < V, T > W > X. Conclusions: I. V > T II. S > R. Which conclusion is true?

options.A: Either I or II is true
options.D: Both I and II are true
options.E: Neither I nor II is true

questions.explanation: T < Q = R < P < V, so V > T. S >= T does not prove S > R.

questions.question: Statements: Some ledgers are files. All files are records. No record is deleted. Conclusions: I. Some ledgers are records. II. No file is deleted.
questions.explanation: Some ledgers are files and all files are records, so some ledgers are records. Since no record is deleted, no file is deleted.

questions.question: A person moves 6 m north, 8 m east and 6 m south. What is the shortest distance from the starting point?
questions.explanation: North and south movement cancel; only 8 m east remains.

questions.question: In a code language, 'data strong file secure' is written as 'ra mi lo ki', 'internet access strong code' is 'no pa mi tu', and 'digital backup file code' is 'xu tu lo sa'. What is the code for 'file'?
questions.explanation: 'File' appears in statements 1 and 3; the common code is 'lo'.

questions.question: Series: D 3 P M 9 A Z % X 2 5 @ K C 6 * T 7 Q. Which element is fifth to the right of the eleventh element from the right end?
questions.explanation: The eleventh from the right is X; fifth to its right is 7.

questions.question: In the word MONETARY, how many pairs of letters have as many letters between them in the word as in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: Checking forward and backward positions gives two valid alphabetical pairs.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: GKI, NRP, LPN, TXV, PTS
questions.explanation: In GKI, NRP, LPN and TXV the first-to-second jump is +4 and second-to-third is -2. PTS does not follow it.

questions.question: If A > B = C >= D < E, which statement is definitely true?
questions.explanation: A > B = C and C >= D, so A > D is definite.

questions.question: Statements: All apps are tools. Some tools are secure. Conclusions: I. Some secure are apps. II. Some tools are apps.
questions.explanation: All apps are tools implies some tools are apps. No definite relation between secure and apps exists.

questions.question: Six persons J, K, L, M, N and P have different heights. J is taller than K but shorter than L. M is taller than L. P is shorter than K but taller than N. Who is the shortest?
questions.explanation: The order includes M > L > J > K > P > N.

questions.question: Question: Is X older than Y? Statement I: X is older than Z. Statement II: Z is older than Y.
questions.explanation: Together X > Z > Y, so X is older than Y.

questions.question: What comes next: BEK, DGM, FIO, HKQ, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter position increases by two.

questions.question: Find the missing number: 4, 9, 19, 39, 79, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is multiplied by 2 and then 1 is added.

questions.question: Find the wrong number in the series: 3, 6, 18, 108, 648, 7776
questions.explanation: The multipliers should be 2, 3, 6, 12, so after 108 the next term should be 1296, not 648.

questions.question: If North is called East, East is called South, South is called West and West is called North, in which direction is the sun seen at sunrise?
questions.explanation: Sunrise is actually in the East, and East is called South.

questions.question: If BANK is coded as DCPM, how is LOAN coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted two places forward.

questions.question: P, Q, R, S and T attend seminars in January to May. R attends before S but after P. Q attends immediately before T. If P attends in February, who attends in April?
questions.explanation: P is February, R March, Q April, T May, and S must be after R? The fixed immediate pair makes Q in April.

questions.question: Statement: Several customers reported failed ATM withdrawals but debit entries were made. Course I: The bank should investigate transaction logs. Course II: The bank should disable all ATMs permanently. Which follows?
questions.explanation: Investigating logs is reasonable; disabling all ATMs permanently is extreme.

questions.question: A report says mobile banking complaints increased after new app features were added. Which statement weakens the conclusion that the features caused complaints?

options.B: The bank also doubled its active app users during the same month.
options.D: Some complaints were about branch timing.
options.E: The app had a new colour theme.

questions.explanation: More users can increase complaint count even if the complaint rate did not worsen.

questions.question: How many meaningful English words can be formed from the letters A, T, E using each letter once?
questions.explanation: ATE and EAT are meaningful words.

questions.question: If all digits in 579248 are arranged in descending order, what is the difference between the second digit from left and the third digit from right?
questions.explanation: Descending order is 987542. The second digit from the left is 8 and the third digit from the right is 5. Difference = 3.

questions.question: If each vowel in the word FINANCE is changed to the next letter and each consonant to the previous letter, what will be the second letter from the left?
questions.explanation: F becomes E, I becomes J, so the second letter is J.

questions.question: There are five females in a family. M is mother of N. O is sister of N. P is daughter of O. Q is mother of M. How many female members are certainly there?
questions.explanation: M, O, P and Q are female; the statement says there are five females, so the answer is five.

questions.question: Eight designations are in decreasing seniority: Chairman, MD, GM, DGM, SM, Manager, AM, Clerk. G is three designations senior to D. D is Assistant Manager. What is G's designation?
questions.explanation: Three levels senior to Assistant Manager are Manager, Senior Manager and Deputy General Manager.
